known_limitations_and_risks: Philox KAT vectors and the citation path tests/kat_vectors are from memory (carried over from study 001), not from a downloaded file.

Runtime identity C1 (INFO/NONINFO coupling until the first effective decoy) is a strengthening added by the implementer to enforce spec fixtures 3-4 in every block; a reviewer must confirm it is a deterministic consequence of the frozen design and cannot fail on a correct run.

Decoupling is defined as the first update at which some NONINFO decoy probe differs from the true cache; decoy applications at weights 0 and 32 (and accidental fixed patterns of the permutation) do not decouple.
The 'shared permutation identifier' in candidate rows is the index block*256+update-1 into the separate 416-byte audit permutation file, not an inline copy of the permutation.
Rejected DECOY_PERMUTATION and survival values are not stored; the analyzer verifies accepted values only. An auditor can regenerate rejected values from Philox and the key derivation.
Donor tie-breaks by 64-bit donor key are not stored in audit rows; the analyzer checks only that the donor has minimal mismatch. An auditor can regenerate donor keys from Philox.

The C++ collision audit enumerates seven representative blocks and survival/decoy retries 0-3. Coverage of all blocks and retries rests on counters carrying block, update, step and retry verbatim, which is checked.
The 12 absolute cell-mean records carry no inferential bound because none is frozen; they are labelled descriptive.
Analyzer validation is strict, and any mismatch is a terminal INVALID after production. An analyzer bug found only after production would close the route.
The per-update record grew from 24 to 48 bytes and the audit row from 72 to 88 bytes; projected output is 4,229,120,000 bytes (about 3.94 GiB), within the 50 GiB driver limit and the 100 GiB ceiling.
Binary and helper names keep the study-001 mmem_ prefix to preserve the accepted file set and Makefile.
std::filesystem on GCC 8 needs -lstdc++fs; unsigned __int128 is used only for an optional fixture cross-check.
